tasks.gr6-shapes-t3: Topic: Properties of 2D shapes and 3D objects. Cover identifying polygons (triangle to octagon), counting sides and angles, and properties of 3D objects (faces, edges, vertices) including cubes, cylinders, cones, spheres, and pyramids. Ask Grade 6 learners to identify shapes, state properties, and distinguish 2D from 3D.
tasks.gr6-symmetry-t3: Topic: Symmetry and reflections. Cover lines of symmetry, counting lines of symmetry in shapes, reflections across vertical and horizontal axes, and identifying symmetrical figures. Ask Grade 6 learners to identify lines of symmetry, draw reflection images, and explain symmetry in shapes.
tasks.gr6-length-t3: Topic: Length and measurement. Cover units of length (millimetres, centimetres, metres, kilometres), converting between units, choosing appropriate units, and estimating lengths. Ask Grade 6 learners to convert between length units, choose sensible units, and solve length calculation problems.
tasks.gr6-area-perimeter-t3: Topic: Area and perimeter. Cover the meaning of perimeter (boundary length) and area (surface covered), formulas for rectangles and squares, and solving problems. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate perimeter and area of rectangles and squares, distinguish between area and perimeter, and apply correct units.
tasks.gr6-volume-t3: Topic: Volume of 3D objects. Cover the meaning of volume, cubic centimetres, the formula length × breadth × height, and counting unit cubes. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate volume using the formula, count unit cubes, and apply volume in practical contexts.
tasks.gr6-add-subtract-6digit-t3: Topic: Adding and subtracting whole numbers up to 6 digits, and problems. Cover estimating by rounding to the nearest 10 000 or 100 000, column addition and subtraction including borrowing across zeros, the properties of addition, compensating, and problems: summation, a missing part, increase and decrease, comparison by difference and finding the original amount. Write numbers with a space between groups of three digits (469 134) and rand amounts as R224 442. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate and to choose the operation that a problem needs, with whole-number answers.
tasks.gr6-percentages-t3: Topic: Percentages (new in Grade 6). Cover per cent as out of 100, tenths and hundredths as percentages (3/10 = 30%, 7/100 = 7%), fractions whose denominators are factors of 100 (1/2, 1/4, 3/4, 1/5, 1/20, 1/25, 1/50), decimals in tenths and hundredths as percentages (0,3 = 30%, 0,25 = 25%), and a percentage of a whole number using the fraction route (25% of R300 = 1/4 of R300 = R75) and 10% first, including simple discounts. Do not ask learners to change any other fraction (such as 1/3 or 1/8) into a percentage. Write rand amounts as R75 and numbers with a space between groups of three digits. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate with whole-number or whole-rand answers.
tasks.gr6-temperature-t3: Topic: Temperature. Cover degrees Celsius, the temperatures worth knowing (water freezes at 0 degrees, a healthy body is about 37 degrees, water boils at 100 degrees), reading analogue thermometers on numbered and un-numbered lines and digital thermometers with a decimal (36,7), comparing and ordering temperatures, differences, and rises and falls, using positive whole numbers and decimals only. Write temperatures as 26 °C and 36,7 °C with a decimal comma. Ask Grade 6 learners to read, compare and calculate.
tasks.gr6-transformations-t3: Topic: Transformations used to describe patterns. Cover translation (sliding without turning or flipping), reflection (a mirror image over a line, each point the same distance from the line on the other side), rotation (turning about a centre; a quarter turn, four quarter turns make a full turn), and lines of symmetry in patterns from nature, everyday life and cultural heritage (honeycomb, bead bracelets, doilies, windmills). Learners describe patterns; they do not draw tessellations. Locate points with alpha-numeric grid references (letter for the column then the number of the row) and describe the grid in the question because there is no picture. Ask Grade 6 learners to name the transformation or give the new position.
tasks.gr6-viewing-objects-t3: Topic: Viewing objects (position and views). Cover matching views with the position of the viewer (front, back, left, right, above) for everyday objects (a tin of beans is a cylinder, a party hat a cone, a dice a cube), collections of objects, and composite geometric objects made of cubes in towers. Describe a structure in words (towers of 3, 1 and 2 cubes from left to right as seen from the front) because there is no picture: the back view reverses the order, the side view of a row one cube deep shows only the tallest tower, and from the side of a two-row structure the viewer sees the tallest tower in each row, the front row on the viewer's left when looking from the right. Ask Grade 6 learners to list a view from left to right, count cubes, match a view to the viewer's position, or name the flat shape seen.
